baslik: What If You Rode for the Pony Express in 1860?
ozet: Spring 1860. Riders must weigh under 125 pounds, the pay beats a carpenter's many times over, and you swear an oath with a Bible in your hand. A fresh horse every few miles, 1,900 miles in ten days, and a leather mail pouch you are told to protect with your life. This is what it was really like to ride for the Pony Express.

kesitler.baslik: The Pony Express Job Ad Was Probably Fake
The Leather Bag Worth More Than the Rider
340 Miles Without Rest, Then He Fell Asleep in the Saddle

kapak_sahne: The young rider from the reference image galloping straight toward the viewer on a small fast brown horse across an empty prairie at sunset, a leather mail cover on the saddle, dust flying, his scarf streaming behind him, determined look.
stil: Minimalist 2D animated short film still. Flat cartoon, clean thin black outlines. High-contrast cinematic chiaroscuro lighting, deep black and charcoal shadows, limited palette of charcoal, cream and warm amber light, glow around light sources, subtle film grain, 16:9 wide composition with lots of negative space. No text, no letters, no writing
insan: People, and only people, are drawn as simple cartoon characters with big round cream-white heads, small black dot eyes, thick expressive black eyebrows, no nose, simple rounded bodies

karakterler.sen: one skinny young man about eighteen, an 1860 express rider: short straw-coloured hair, wide-brimmed tan hat, red bandana scarf around his neck, brown leather vest over a light blue shirt, dark trousers tucked into tall brown boots
karakterler.majors: one 1860 businessman about forty-five: dark hair, full dark beard, black frock coat, white shirt, black bow tie
karakterler.keeper: one 1860 frontier station keeper: grey stubble beard, rolled-up shirt sleeves, brown work apron, battered grey hat

bloklar.anlatim: Spring, 1860. St. Joseph, Missouri. You are young, you are skinny, and you can ride. And for the first time in your life, being small is exactly what someone is looking for.

sahneler.tarif: A small 1860 river town at dusk, wooden and brick buildings without any signs along a muddy street, a wide river behind, lamps in windows.
The young rider from the reference image standing next to a much bigger, broad-shouldered man with a round cream head in a line of men outside a stable, looking up at him.

bloklar.anlatim: A new company needs riders who weigh no more than a hundred and twenty-five pounds. Every pound you don't weigh is a pound the horse doesn't have to carry.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image standing on a big old iron weighing scale in a stable while a man with a round cream head squints at the needle.

bloklar.anlatim: You may have heard about their famous job advert. Wanted: young, skinny, wiry fellows, not over eighteen. Must be expert riders, willing to risk death daily. Orphans preferred.

sahneler.tarif: An old paper notice nailed to a wooden post, covered only in grey blurred blocks instead of words, flapping in the wind.
sahneler.i2v: The paper notice flaps in the wind, the grass around the post sways. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: It's a great story. It's also probably a hoax. Nobody has ever found that ad in the newspapers of the time.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image shrugging with both palms up, standing next to the wooden post.

bloklar.anlatim: The pay is real, though. More than a hundred dollars a month. An unskilled labourer is lucky to make a dollar a day. A carpenter, less than two.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image holding a small cloth bag of coins in both hands, staring at it in disbelief.
A tired carpenter with a round cream head sawing a plank in a dusty workshop, a few coins on the bench.
sahneler.i2v: He saws the plank back and forth slowly, sawdust falls. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: There's a catch. Alexander Majors, one of the owners, is a religious man. He hands you a Bible, and you sign an oath. No swearing. No liquor. No fighting with the other men.

sahneler.tarif: The bearded businessman from the reference image handing a small leather Bible across a desk, very serious, lamp light.
The young rider from the reference image signing a paper with a pen at the desk, his other hand on a small Bible.

bloklar.anlatim: Here's why they need you. After gold was discovered in California, thousands rushed west. By 1860, California has three hundred and eighty thousand people. And they want their mail, fast.

sahneler.tarif: A crowded 1860 California street of wooden buildings without signs, people with round cream heads everywhere, hills behind.
sahneler.i2v: The people walk and bustle along the street, dust rises in the sunlight. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: A sack of letters slumped in a dusty corner of a stagecoach office, cobwebs on it.

bloklar.anlatim: The plan: carry the mail on horseback from St. Joseph, Missouri, to Sacramento, California. About one thousand, nine hundred miles. In ten days. Many people said it was impossible.

sahneler.tarif: A plain map-like drawing of the western United States with no writing, a glowing amber line stretching from the Missouri River across plains, mountains and desert to California.
Two skeptical businessmen with round cream heads in top hats laughing and shaking their heads at a table.

bloklar.anlatim: Three businessmen, Russell, Majors and Waddell, set the whole thing up in two months. Riders, stations, and hundreds of horses.

sahneler.tarif: The bearded businessman from the reference image with two other businessmen with round cream heads leaning over a big map spread on a table, lamp light.

bloklar.anlatim: They were already in the freighting business. At their peak, they employed six thousand men and owned seventy-five thousand oxen.

sahneler.tarif: A long line of covered freight wagons pulled by teams of oxen across a dusty plain at sunset.
sahneler.i2v: The oxen pull the wagons slowly forward, dust rises in the golden light. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Sending a letter will cost five dollars, for half an ounce. That's about a hundred and eighty dollars today. Regular mail costs two cents.

sahneler.tarif: A single thin envelope on one side of an old brass balance scale and a heavy pile of coins on the other side.
A well-dressed banker with a round cream head reluctantly handing over a coin at a counter to send one small letter.

bloklar.anlatim: April 3, 1860. The first mail is coming from New York and Washington by train. And it's late. The messenger missed a connection in Detroit.

sahneler.tarif: A railway platform at evening with a crowd of people with round cream heads looking down an empty track, checking pocket watches.

bloklar.anlatim: So the railroad clears the track and sends a special locomotive with one car. It crosses Missouri, two hundred and six miles, in a record four hours and fifty-one minutes.

sahneler.tarif: An 1860 steam locomotive with a tall smokestack pulling a single car at full speed across open country at sunset.
sahneler.i2v: The locomotive races forward, thick smoke pours from the stack, the wheels spin. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: Close view of the big wheels and pistons of an old steam locomotive in motion, sparks and steam.

bloklar.anlatim: In St. Joseph, a crowd is waiting. The mayor gives a speech. Then the owners give speeches.

sahneler.tarif: A big crowd of people with round cream heads in a town square at dusk, a man with a round cream head on a wooden platform waving his arms in a speech, flags and lanterns.
sahneler.i2v: The speaker waves his arms, the crowd shifts and claps, the flags flutter. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: At about a quarter past seven in the evening, the mail pouch is handed to the first rider. A cannon fires. The crowd cheers. And he's off.

sahneler.tarif: A small old cannon firing a big puff of white smoke at dusk.
sahneler.i2v: White smoke bursts and billows out of the cannon, the smoke drifts away. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: A young rider with a round cream head on a small fast brown horse galloping away down a crowded street at dusk, the crowd cheering on both sides.

bloklar.anlatim: Inside the pouch: forty-nine letters, five private telegrams, and some papers for San Francisco and towns along the way.

sahneler.tarif: A leather mail pouch opened on a table, a small neat bundle of envelopes and folded papers inside, lamp light.

bloklar.anlatim: Who was that first rider? Nobody is completely sure. Most historians say Johnny Fry or Billy Richardson. He rode straight onto a waiting ferry and crossed the Missouri River into Kansas.

sahneler.tarif: A paddle-wheel steam ferry crossing a wide dark river at night, a rider and his horse standing on its deck, lanterns glowing.
sahneler.i2v: The paddle wheel turns, the ferry moves across the river, the lantern light glimmers on the water. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Meanwhile, in Sacramento, a rider named Sam Hamilton set off with the first mail going the other way.

sahneler.tarif: A lone rider with a round cream head galloping out of a sleeping riverside town at night, a single lamp behind him.
sahneler.i2v: The rider gallops away into the dark, the lamp glows behind him. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Now it's your turn. Your job is one stretch of the route, usually seventy-five to a hundred miles. Day or night. In any weather.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image on a small fast brown horse galloping across a vast empty 1860 prairie of tall grass under a huge sky at dawn, his scarf flying behind him.
sahneler.i2v: The horse gallops forward, the tall grass sways, his scarf flies in the wind. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image riding hunched against heavy rain at night on a muddy trail.

bloklar.anlatim: Every ten to fifteen miles, there's a station. You jump off, grab a fresh horse, maybe a bite to eat, and you're gone again.

sahneler.tarif: A small lonely log cabin station with a corral on an empty plain, one fresh saddled horse tied to the fence, smoke from the chimney.
sahneler.i2v: Smoke rises from the chimney, the tied horse shifts its weight and swishes its tail. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image leaping from one horse onto another beside the corral fence while the station keeper from the reference image holds the reins.

bloklar.anlatim: On a single run, you'll change horses eight to ten times. Most of the way, you're at a fast canter. Sometimes, a full gallop, up to twenty-five miles an hour.

sahneler.tarif: Low view of a small fast brown horse at full gallop, hooves kicking up dust, the rider leaning low over its neck.
sahneler.i2v: The horse gallops at full speed, its legs pound, dust flies up behind it. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: The only thing you take with you is the mochila. A leather cover thrown over the saddle, with four locked pockets full of mail. You sit on it. That's what holds it in place.

sahneler.tarif: Close view of a leather saddle cover with four box-shaped leather pockets with small padlocks, thrown over a saddle, warm light.
The young rider from the reference image swinging the leather saddle cover from one saddle onto another in one quick move.

bloklar.anlatim: Your bosses are very clear about it. If it comes to it, the horse and rider should perish before the mail does.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image gulping nervously, clutching the leather saddle cover against his chest.

bloklar.anlatim: To save weight, almost everything is gone. In the end, besides the mail, you carry one revolver and a water sack.

sahneler.tarif: A small water sack and an old revolver lying on a wooden bench next to the leather mail cover, nothing else.

bloklar.anlatim: Even the saddles were special. A saddle maker in St. Joseph, Israel Landis, built them with less leather, less metal and less wood, to save weight.

sahneler.tarif: A small saddle maker's workshop with leather hides and tools on the walls, a craftsman with a round cream head stitching a light saddle by lamp light.
sahneler.i2v: He pulls the stitching thread through the leather, the lamp flame flickers. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: And the horses? The company paid around two hundred dollars each. They're small and fast, about nine hundred pounds. That's where the name pony comes from, even if not all of them really are.

sahneler.tarif: A corral full of small fast horses of different colours at sunset, kicking up dust.
sahneler.i2v: The horses trot around the corral, dust rises in the golden light. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: The route follows the Oregon and California trails. Across the plains of Kansas and Nebraska, past a tall spire of rock called Chimney Rock.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image on horseback, tiny in the distance, riding past a tall thin spire of rock rising from the plain at sunset.
sahneler.i2v: The rider moves slowly across the plain, the grass sways, the sunset clouds drift. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Then up the Sweetwater River, past Independence Rock, and through South Pass.

sahneler.tarif: A huge rounded granite rock rising from a grassy valley beside a small river, morning light.
A wide high mountain pass between snowy peaks, a single rider crossing it far away.
sahneler.i2v: Clouds drift over the snowy peaks, the grass in the pass ripples in the wind. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Down to Salt Lake City. Then across the Great Basin, the desert of Utah and Nevada, where some stations stand in remote places with no one else around for miles.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image on horseback crossing a flat white desert under a blazing sun, heat shimmer, distant bare mountains.
sahneler.i2v: Heat shimmers above the desert floor, the horse trots steadily forward. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: A tiny stone station hut alone in an endless empty desert at dusk.

bloklar.anlatim: Then over the Sierra Nevada, near Lake Tahoe, and down to Sacramento.

sahneler.tarif: A deep blue mountain lake surrounded by pine forest and granite peaks, a narrow trail along the shore.
sahneler.i2v: The lake water ripples, the pine trees sway gently, clouds drift over the peaks. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: The first westbound mail reaches Sacramento at one in the morning on April 14. Ten days, as promised. From there, a steamer carries it down the river to San Francisco.

sahneler.tarif: A riverside town at night, a rider with a round cream head pulling up his tired horse in front of a lit office, a small cheering crowd.
A paddle steamer with glowing windows moving down a dark river at night.
sahneler.i2v: The steamer moves slowly down the river, the paddle wheel turns, the lights reflect on the water. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: In San Francisco, the first pouch was delivered around midnight. Inside was a letter of congratulations from President Buchanan to the governor of California. Eighty-five pieces of mail in all.

sahneler.tarif: A foggy San Francisco waterfront at midnight, a small crowd of people with round cream heads holding lanterns around a rider and his horse.
sahneler.i2v: The lanterns sway, the fog drifts, the horse shakes its mane. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: This job is dangerous. In May 1860, the Paiute War broke out in Nevada. Pony Express stations were attacked.

sahneler.tarif: A lonely desert station at night with a red glow on the horizon, smoke rising in the distance.
sahneler.i2v: Smoke rises slowly into the night sky, the red glow flickers on the horizon. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Sixteen employees were killed, and around a hundred and fifty horses were taken or driven off. For the only time in its history, the Pony Express had to stop. The mail did not go through.

sahneler.tarif: An empty corral with a broken gate swinging in the wind at dawn, no horses.
sahneler.i2v: The broken gate swings slowly in the wind, dust blows across the empty corral. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

sahneler.tarif: A stack of mail pouches piled up untouched in a dark station room.

bloklar.anlatim: One pouch that left San Francisco that July didn't reach its destination for almost two years.

sahneler.tarif: A single dusty leather mail pouch lying forgotten on a shelf, cobwebs on it.

bloklar.anlatim: And then there were riders like Pony Bob Haslam. When the next rider refused to go on, Bob took the mail himself. Then he rode back with the westbound mail.

sahneler.tarif: A tough young rider with a round cream head and a red scarf taking a mail pouch from a frightened rider in a station doorway, lamp light.
A lone rider galloping through a dark rocky canyon at night under the stars.
sahneler.i2v: The rider gallops forward through the canyon, the stars glitter, dust rises. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Along the way, an arrow struck his jaw, and he lost three teeth. He finished anyway. Three hundred and eighty miles, round trip. The longest ride on record.

sahneler.tarif: A tired rider with a round cream head and a bandaged jaw slumped in the saddle of a walking horse at dawn, arriving at a station.

bloklar.anlatim: If a rider can't go on, someone has to ride double. Jack Keetley once rode three hundred and forty miles in thirty-one hours, without stopping to rest or eat.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image riding through the night under a full moon, swaying, eyes half closed, slumping lower and lower in the saddle.
sahneler.i2v: He sways in the saddle as the horse walks on, the moonlit grass ripples. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: When he finally arrived, he was taken from the saddle sound asleep.

sahneler.tarif: Two station hands with round cream heads gently lifting a sleeping rider down from his horse at dawn, his hat falling off.

bloklar.anlatim: Mark Twain, in his travel memoir Roughing It, described the rider as usually a little bit of a man.

sahneler.tarif: A stagecoach on a dusty road, a passenger with a round cream head leaning out of the window and watching a small rider gallop past.
sahneler.i2v: The rider gallops past the stagecoach, dust rises, the stagecoach rolls slowly. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: And Buffalo Bill Cody later told many stories of his time as a Pony Express rider. Some of them may have been made up, or at least exaggerated.

sahneler.tarif: A big theatrical tent show at night with bright lanterns, a showman with a round cream head and long hair in a fringed jacket waving a big hat on a horse in the arena.

bloklar.anlatim: In November 1860, you carry the biggest news of the year. Abraham Lincoln has won the election.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image galloping through falling snow on a white trail, a leather mail cover on his saddle.
sahneler.i2v: Snow falls, the horse gallops forward, snow flies up from its hooves. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: Four years earlier, it had taken months for news of the last election to reach the West. This time, California's newspapers have the result seven days and seventeen hours after the East Coast papers.

sahneler.tarif: A busy 1860 newspaper print shop at night, workers with round cream heads pulling fresh blank pages from a press.
sahneler.i2v: The press moves up and down, fresh blank pages come out, the lamps glow. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: But something faster is coming. All along the route, men are putting up poles and stringing wire. The telegraph.

sahneler.tarif: A long line of wooden telegraph poles stretching across an empty plain to the horizon, a work wagon and men with round cream heads raising one more pole.
The young rider from the reference image on horseback stopping beside a telegraph pole, looking up at the wire.

bloklar.anlatim: On October 24, 1861, the telegraph reaches Salt Lake City, connecting Omaha and Sacramento. Two days later, the Pony Express announces it is closing.

sahneler.tarif: Close view of a telegraph key and a coil of wire on a wooden desk, a single lamp.
A telegraph wire humming against a grey sky, a small bird sitting on it.
sahneler.i2v: The wire vibrates slightly, the bird shifts its feet, grey clouds drift. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: It lasted about eighteen months. It carried around thirty-five thousand letters. And it lost money. It made ninety thousand dollars and lost two hundred thousand.

sahneler.tarif: The bearded businessman from the reference image sitting alone at a desk at night with an open ledger, his head in his hands.

bloklar.anlatim: Because sending a letter was so expensive, very little of that mail survives. Only about two hundred and fifty pieces are known today.

sahneler.tarif: A single old envelope in a glass display case in a dark museum, lit by one small spotlight.

bloklar.anlatim: In 1869, the Pony Express became the first real historic event ever shown on a United States postage stamp. Before that, stamps showed only the faces of presidents and founders.

sahneler.tarif: A small postage stamp with a plain drawing of a galloping horse and rider, no letters or numbers, lying on a dark desk.

bloklar.anlatim: Today, the old route is a National Historic Trail, running through eight states.

sahneler.tarif: An empty dirt trail winding across a wide prairie toward distant mountains, a small wooden marker post without any writing beside it, golden afternoon light.
sahneler.i2v: The grass sways in the wind beside the trail, clouds drift over the mountains. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.

bloklar.anlatim: So, honest question. Over a hundred dollars a month, a fresh horse every fifteen miles, and a leather bag you're supposed to protect with your life. Would you have signed the oath? Tell me in the comments.

sahneler.tarif: The young rider from the reference image sitting on his horse at sunset, holding up the leather mail cover and looking straight at the viewer with a questioning look, the empty prairie behind him.
sahneler.i2v: His scarf moves in the wind, the horse shifts slightly, the grass sways in the sunset light. Flat 2D cartoon animation, static camera.
